items.title: Bob Magnusson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: Principal clarinetist. And she kind of was very protective of him from us.

ctx.x: Were your kids aware of what you did for a living, and did they think it was out of the ordinary?

No I don’t think so. And my wife, she was always, and is, very, you know, the trash has to go out and the bed isn’t made here and the kids need this. So it kept me in the real dad thing, which I’m really grateful for to her. I know with my mother and dad, my dad, playing in an orchestra is a huge amount of pressure. Principal clarinetist. And she kind of was very protective of him from us. You know, “Oh now don’t upset your dad, he’s got to play tonight.” And some of that is good and there’s times when yeah you…

Cool. Yeah, mentioning being a principal anything in a symphony, that’s such a totally different kind of pressure, like every note has to be — the idea of mistake is so small. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
